content.MEASURED_ON_A_DIFFERENT_POPULATION: THE NUMBERS BELOW WERE MEASURED ON THE THREE-ARM DATASET (n_rows_in_dataset 645,851), NOT on this receipt's population (btc score 311,640 rows / 177,674 actions, fit 577,598; eth score 299,703 / 260,602). They have NOT been re-measured here. Carrying the magnitudes across populations without saying so would attach one dataset's figures to another's receipt, so they are fenced rather than restated as current.

content.WHAT_TRANSFERS_REGARDLESS_OF_POPULATION: The MECHANISM and the pre-committed reading, which do not depend on the magnitude: every arm is scored on the IDENTICAL row set, so any post-gap queue unreliability is COMMON-MODE and cannot move a PAIRED comparison between arms. That reading was committed in Q-DA-79(5) BEFORE the number existed, precisely so it could not be inflated afterwards. It holds for this receipt on the same argument. What does NOT transfer is the claim '0.030% of rows' -- that is a measurement of another dataset.
content.authorised_by: R-173(2); design/metric/null/falsifier declared in Q-DA-79 BEFORE any data was read
content.consequence_for_phase2: NONE on the common-mode argument (see WHAT_TRANSFERS_REGARDLESS_OF_POPULATION). The arms' ranking stands unqualified on this account. The magnitude on THIS population is UNMEASURED, not zero.
content.finding: H0 FALSIFIED, BUT SHALLOW AND NEGLIGIBLE IN MAGNITUDE.
content.forward_refinement_not_retroactive: POST_GAP_QUEUE_UNRELIABLE remains a pre-declared refinement for FUTURE builds only. R-173(2) is explicit that this never becomes a retroactive edit to a built population, and nothing here proposes one.
content.interpretation: The exposure is REAL but SHALLOW. 195 of 645,851 rows (0.030%) are admitted OK while preceding their own book resync. Median and p90 resync lag both round to -0.0 s: almost every exposed row sits within milliseconds of the resync instant, and only the extreme tail reaches 1.135 s. EVERY gap was followed by a snapshot (0 slugs left unresynced), so there is no persistent unresynced state anywhere in the population. btc-only, because eth carries no PM gaps in this top-up.
content.question: R-173 ruled a PM gap excludes ROWS, not the window. Rows INSIDE a gap carry GAP_IN_HORIZON. This asked about rows AFTER a gap: queue-ahead needs book state, and BookState refuses to mutate until a full post-gap snapshot arrives, so a row can report status=OK while its qahead rests on a book that was never re-established. The status field describes the FILL HORIZON and says nothing about queue validity, which is why this could hide.
content.reading_PRE_COMMITTED_BEFORE_THE_NUMBER_: Q-DA-79(5), filed before this ran: Phase 2's gate is a PAIRED comparison on identical rows and all three arms see the same post-gap rows, so any unreliability is COMMON-MODE. A large exposed set would QUALIFY WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN and would NOT invalidate the ranking between arms. At 0.030% of rows it cannot move a paired comparison at all. This reading was committed in advance precisely so it could not be inflated afterwards.

secondary_reported_without_test.note: Declared in Q-DA-79 as side-by-side with NO test, and reported that way. Directionally consistent with a stale book inflating queue-ahead; it is NOT a tested claim and no inference rests on it.
